html:
Saint Sava was the first archbishop of the independent Serbian Orthodox Church, born around 1174 as Rastko, the youngest son of Stefan Nemanja.

He ran away as a teenager to become a monk on Mount Athos, where he founded Hilandar monastery with his father. In 1219 he won from the patriarch at Nicaea the right for Serbia to have its own church, and he became its first archbishop, with his seat at Žiča. He wrote the first Serbian law book for the church, a life of his father and rules for monasteries. The Ottomans burned his relics in Belgrade in 1594. He is the patron of Serbian schools, and the huge Church of Saint Sava in Belgrade honours him. The church he founded kept Serbian identity alive under Ottoman rule.
sum: Saint Sava was the first archbishop of the independent Serbian Orthodox Church, born around 1174 as Rastko, the youngest son of Stefan Nemanja.
